findings.evidence: template/scripts/model_routing.py:990–1003 accepts failed/abnormal execution based only on matching task content, without checking execution.violation or verified recovery. prepare then replaces the route and takes a fresh integration snapshot (line 964). Consequently, a child that modified integration state can be re-routed as complex; record_retained_execution (1503–1508) checks against that new snapshot, treating the escaped writes as pre-existing, and require_routing_gate accepts the retained outcome. This bypasses the existing evidence-bound containment recovery.
findings.summary: Re-routing a failed Codex child can erase an unresolved containment violation and allow terminal completion.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/model_routing.py:990–1003 does not reject execution.writer_state == 'ambiguous'. delegated_write_guard.py:690–705 records that state when the child's process group survives cleanup. If task content momentarily matches the recorded post-snapshot, prepare permits a complex retained route, which launches no child and therefore bypasses _WriterOwnership.acquire. record_retained_execution's postcheck (model_routing.py:1516–1522) checks integration content only, allowing completion without proving the old task-worktree writer has stopped.
findings.summary: The new re-route exception permits supervisor retention while a failed child may still own the worktree.
